subject: Medford Square District Improvement Financing Master Plan
overview: The council approved a District Improvement Financing (DIF) master plan for Medford Square on first reading and adopted a state-level specialized energy code for new construction. Members also debated a proposed deed restriction amendment for family-supportive housing and referred a major affordable housing zoning amendment to the Community Development Board.

items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions and Meeting Records
items.summary: The council congratulated Ray and Maureen Brady on their 70th wedding anniversary, recognized the Jewish high holidays, and approved the records of the September 5, 2023 meeting.

items.title: Committee Reports
items.summary: Approved reports from the Committee of the Whole and the Zoning Planning and Development Subcommittee regarding District Improvement Financing, Walkling Court, and a draft Condo Conversion Ordinance.

items.title: Executive Session: DuPont v. City of Medford
items.summary: Entered executive session to discuss strategy regarding pending litigation in the matter of DuPont versus City of Medford.

items.title: Public Hearings for Extended Business Hours
items.summary: Approved special permits for Matsuba Izakaya and Domino's to operate with extended late-night hours, subject to 30- and 60-day reviews for neighborhood impacts.

items.title: Medford Square District Improvement Financing (DIF)
items.summary: Approved on first reading a master plan to implement a DIF district in Medford Square to capture tax increments for infrastructure and water-sewer upgrades. Supporters viewed the tool as a necessary stimulus for development, while opponents criticized the lack of a broader city-wide comprehensive plan and questioned the projected return on investment.

items.title: Walkling Court Zoning Amendment Referral
items.summary: Referred a proposed zoning amendment for the Medford Housing Authority's Walkling Court affordable housing project to the Community Development Board for a public hearing.

items.title: 12 Dell Avenue Deed Restriction Amendment
items.summary: Tabled a request to amend a city-held deed restriction at 12 Dell Avenue until October 24 to allow the administration and petitioner to negotiate terms for a proposed family-supportive housing structure. Discussion focused on the potential for a developer windfall versus the private needs of the family, as well as fire department access and ledge removal concerns.

items.title: Field and Park Maintenance
items.summary: Requested that the Parks Department repair the Brooks School mini soccer field turf following reports of seams ripping and safety concerns for young players.

items.title: Commercial Truck Parking Issues
items.summary: Requested that the administration address persistent overnight and daytime commercial truck and tractor-trailer parking issues on city streets such as Commercial Street and Ring Road.

items.title: Rodent Infestation Mitigation
items.summary: Referred a resolution concerning worsening rodent infestations to a committee meeting with the Health Department to develop a city-wide mitigation plan.

items.title: Adoption of Specialized Energy Code
items.summary: Approved the first reading of an ordinance adopting the state's Specialized Energy Code to require higher efficiency and passive house standards for new construction. Councilor Scarpelli recused himself from the matter due to a professional conflict of interest.

items.title: McGlynn Playground ARPA Funding Increase
items.summary: Received a report regarding an increase in ARPA funding for the McGlynn Playground project to over $1 million due to recent bid results.

items.title: Routine Business and Occupancy Limits
items.summary: Accepted a $600 donation for adaptive recreation and referred a request to revise ordinances regarding residential occupancy limits to the Rules and Ordinances subcommittee.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: A resident expressed concerns regarding the Walkling Court development, citing density, the loss of green space, and the health impacts of placing senior housing near active railroad tracks.
